title: THC Antiquities Code Review
permit_name: Antiquities Code Project Review and Antiquities Permit Pathway

source_citations.reference: What to Send In for Project Review

explanations.trigger_explanation: Ground-disturbing work on public land, work by political subdivisions on public land, or work affecting state-owned historic resources commonly triggers Texas Historical Commission Antiquities Code review and can lead to an Antiquities Permit requirement.

known_unknowns: A separate Antiquities Permit is not universal; it depends on whether archaeological investigations or work on a State Antiquities Landmark is needed.
advisories: Additional review recommended early for public-land utility corridors, substations, and water or wastewater infrastructure because archaeological scope can affect sequencing.
notes: Confidence tier 2 because the review requirement is clearly published by the Texas Historical Commission, but the exact permit pathway varies with land status and scope of archaeological work.
